Edward Michael Goldfarb (born July 19, 1966) is an American composer, songwriter, and producer. He is best known for composing the score and songs for the international version of the Pokémon animated television series and films. He has also worked with filmmaker Francis Ford Coppola and produced remixes for artists including Boyz II Men.
Career
Early career
Goldfarb’s professional music career began while he was still in high school. He later worked as assistant music director and pianist for the musical revue Beach Blanket Babylon, where he served as music director for approximately 15 years.
During his time with Beach Blanket Babylon, he worked with numerous entertainers including Bob Hope, Carol Channing, Annette Funicello, Tommy Tune, Tracy Chapman, Alice Walker, Amy Tan, Neil Sedaka, Billy Joe Armstrong, and Adam Savage.
Music production
In the 1990s and 2000s, Goldfarb produced remixes for various artists, including Boyz II Men. He also produced numerous independent albums and collaborated with other musicians on recording projects.
Film, television, and video game scoring
While working at Beach Blanket Babylon, Goldfarb met filmmaker Francis Ford Coppola, who hired him as a music consultant. He worked on films including Jack, Apocalypse Now Redux, Youth Without Youth, and the unproduced Pinocchio.
In 1999, Goldfarb composed the score for the Sony PlayStation video game Monkey Hero.
In 2008, he composed the score for the feature film Hard Scrambled.
Since 2013, Goldfarb has composed the score and songs for the Pokémon franchise, including television episodes and feature films. His work includes composing music for Pokémon the Series: XY Kalos Quest and subsequent seasons, as well as multiple Pokémon films.
Teaching and speaking
Goldfarb served as an adjunct professor at Foothill College in Los Altos, California, from 2010 to 2018. He taught courses including Music Business, Making Music with the Apple iOS, and History of Electronic Music.
He has also appeared as a guest speaker at educational institutions including Stanford University, Sonoma State University, San José State University, and UC Santa Cruz.
Personal life
Goldfarb resides in Marin County, California.
